title: Canonical completeness in the completed integral coefficient presentation
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $X$ any scheme with its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $R_n=(\mathcal O_E/t^n)_X$ and $B=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the canonical identification $B\cong\widehat B=\varprojlim_nR_n$ of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], and the derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K\in D(B)$ and write $\widehat K$ for the same complex after this coefficient identification. For every $n\ge1$ its derived reduction over $\widehat B$, constructed as in [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], is canonically identified with $K_n=K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}R_n$ in $D(R_n)$; these identifications respect quotient transitions and reduction maps from $K$. If $K$ is derived complete in the canonical-map sense of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], the reduction maps of $\widehat K$ form the first map of a distinguished Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]. In the global coefficient setting $\ell\ne p$ this says exactly that $\widehat K$ is derived complete in [def-weil-derived-complete]. No constructibility or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Obtain normalized ordinary integral and finite restriction squares from lem-pe-integral-normalized-restriction-squares. This is coefficient data only; no completeness is used.

Localize the restriction squares. The inverse mate between the actual internal and completed scalar adjunctions is invertible because both encoding functors are equivalences. Postcompose its unit equation by the inverse restriction square to obtain UnitCompatible. To prove uniqueness, transpose any other component under the completed scalar adjunction and cancel that restriction square. This is the private generic mateComparison_existsUnique, specialized by finiteComparison_existsUnique.
Apply lem-pe-integral-reduction-transition-comparison to these unit-normalized comparisons. It supplies the quotient transition equation, completing integral_completion_reduction_comparisons.

Exact countable products of module sheaves give CountableAB4Star, using componentwise epimorphisms and the product comparison for a discrete diagram. The derived countable-product theorem then gives products in the completed scalar derived category. Transport their existence back through A.derived. Unpack canonical completeness into a K-flat representative P, a representative isomorphism e and invertibility of the localized strict augmentation. The declared AdicCompletion.roos_isDerivedLimit supplies its distinguished triangle and the exact equation saying completionMap followed by the first arrow is the product of tensor units.

Use e inverse followed by the invertible strict augmentation as the vertex isomorphism K ≅ Q(roos P). Transport the triangle along this vertex isomorphism and identity product isomorphisms. Its first map is exactly the product of the internal units by the equation in the preceding step, and its third map is delta followed by the shifted inverse vertex isomorphism.

The exact equivalence A.derived preserves countable products, shifts and distinguished triangles. The product comparison followed by the product of the inverse restricted finite comparisons identifies the two product objects. Projectionwise the unit comparison identifies the first arrow, and the transition comparison identifies 1 minus shift. The transported triangle therefore has exactly the first and middle maps of IsSfDerivedComplete. Finally sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy gives each requested global legacy completeness assertion for l != D.p.

proof_origin.place: Coefficient steps 1 and 4 are isolated as separate lemmas; normalized inverse mates, exact product transport and fixed-first-map Roos triangle transport are proved directly in Lean, reusing the declared internal Roos comparison and the proved legacy comparison.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement and inherited searches. Eight steps explicitly identify coefficient actions, K-flat tensor reductions, transition and unit maps, and the strict augmented Roos model; completeness makes its specified augmentation invertible and TR1 gives the required fixed-map triangle. All dependencies already exist; no new nodes. Checked arbitrary schemes and unbounded complexes, and confined the global ell != p convention to the final definitional comparison.
split_report.blueprint: The final comparison sentence in the statement of det-prop-integral-criterion-reductions, realizing sk-prop-integral-criterion step 1: steps 1–4 compare completed coefficient reductions, steps 5–7 identify canonical-map completeness with the required Roos triangle, and step 8 checks the completed-integral convention.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q16-7ea1d549a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Q16 7ea1d549, item lem-pe-integral-completion-presentation. The split has 8 steps and no new nodes; the statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged from the base. The parent det-prop-integral-criterion-reductions cites the item for exactly its two conclusions (same reduction tower; complete K satisfies def-weil-derived-complete). The blueprint source gives no proof of this comparison, so the agent proof origin is right. Small cases checked: K=0, X empty, K=B (L is lim R_n = B-hat), n=1. Step checks: (1) b_n = pi_n alpha and the relabelling is an exact iso of categories. (2) The K-flat test transfers through alpha(U) on presheaf tensors. (3) theta_n is balanced, since alpha(b)p tensor r = p tensor pi_n(alpha(b))r becomes bp tensor r = p tensor b_n(b)r, and it is R_n-linear. (4) The actual transition and unit maps agree (E5). (5) The cone sign was worked out: the inverse rotation of the cone triangle, then (x,y) to (x,-y), gives d(x,y) = (dx,(1-s)x-dy) with j the projection; eta = (gamma,0) is a chain map. (6) The strict-augmentation clause of lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison gives the canonical map; sk-def-pe-derived-completion's own proof also defines it as (c,0). (7) (u,id,id) is a TR1 triangle isomorphism. (8) c_n and t_n match def-weil-integral-reduction-tower and the well-definedness lemma, and the live fixed-first-map def-weil-derived-complete (its blueprint_update is not followed because this delivery does not touch that node). ell != p is used only in step 8. Stacks tags 06YS/06YN/06YT/06YY/0941/08TC/0145 have the cited labels; 06YY and 0941 were read. No SGA source. No duplicate found in the DAG search. Repairs (2, C1/C3): step 6 cited no node for applying sk-def-pe-derived-completion's completeness hypothesis, which is stated for internal module objects with the coequalizer tensor (Layer B), to the item's sectionwise module-sheaf category. Added lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison with det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure and sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor (no cycle; recorded as a tool use). Step 3's canonicity argument assumed a map between any two resolutions; it is replaced by naturality of theta plus the universal property of the clause-(2) left derived functors. Accepted tool uses: lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact, lem-weil-derived-limit-existence, lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison, lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined, lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
